newsitem.title: USA: U.S. FERC slated to decide Primergy merger.
newsitem.headline: U.S. FERC slated to decide Primergy merger.

text.p: The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission Wednesday is scheduled to decide whether to allow a proposed merger between Wisconsin Energy Corp and Northern States Power Co into a holding company called Primergy Corp.

The proposed $6 billion deal between the two upper Midwestern utilities is the biggest the commission has considered since it issued its merger policies in December and would create the nation's tenth largest utility.
The combination would serve more than three million customers in Minnesota, Wisconsin, Michigan, North Dakota and South Dakota.

North Dakota and Michigan regulators have approved the plan, and South Dakota has deferred to the FERC. But Minnesota and Wisconsin public service commissions still have not decided on the controversial proposal.

Minnesota is holding additional hearings and may decide later this summer, while Wisconsin's process hinges on an investigation into whether there was improper contact between a public service commissioner and parties in the case.
The Securities and Exchange Commission and the Justice Department also must rule on the merger, and the Nuclear Regulatory Commission must decide some aspects of it.

A FERC administrative law judge in August approved the merger with conditions, including a four-year freeze on wholesale rates and that Primergy have an independent systems operator (ISO) for scheduling transmission facilities use.
The FERC staff has been concerned that Primergy would have too much market power, and there are questions on whether the commission will push for a stronger, more independent ISO.
